subject: Recap: Post-call — Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Post-call — Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you mentioned:
- High per-request latency on your current in-house reranker, esp. for 2k+ token contexts.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic spikes during batch scoring windows.
- Need for deterministic structured output (JSON) for downstream parsers and auditability.

Goals / success criteria we discussed:
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for single-turn reranking requests at typical payloads.
- Cost: reduce per-call cost ~30% via batching/caching and quantized model options.
- Output: structured JSON with consistent fields for downstream ingestion and telemetry.

Product fit summary (how Redwood helps):
- SDK changes: minimal client-side update. We recommend using Redwood SDK v0.9+ with streaming enabled to get progressive tokens and reduce perceived latency.
- Function calling: use function-calling for deterministic structured outputs; we can surface a typed schema so your parser gets a consistent JSON.
- Streaming: progressive token streaming for long responses (lowers p95) and allows early partial results for UI.
- Structured outputs: Redwood's structured output validation layer can enforce required keys and types before returning final result.
- Embeddings / reranking: suggest a hybrid approach — client-side ANN for candidate retrieval + Redwood embeddings + model-based reranker for final ordering. We can ship a caching layer for repeated queries.

Attachments I included:
- acme-mapping.csv — initial field mapping between your product ontology and the structured output schema.
- redwood-integration-proposal-v1.pdf — implementation plan + proposed timeline and cost estimates.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing):
1) Technical deep-dive (Vivek + engineering) — target week of Nov 9. (Owner: Alex/Sarah to confirm availability)
2) Provide sample payloads and 1k historical queries for benchmark run (Owner: Acme) — target Nov 6.
3) Redwood to run baseline perf & cost analysis and share results + a short PoC plan (Owner: Marissa) — target Nov 13.

Do these look right? If so I’ll lock the deep-dive and share calendar invites.

Thanks again — excited to help optimize this flow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Cost: ballpark (from proposal PDF) for 10M tokens/month is ~$3.2k/month with conservative batching; we’ll run precise numbers after we see the sample traffic profile.

Hi all — quick technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Function calling schema: We recommend a small typed schema for your reranker output: {"top_k": int, "scores": [{"id": string, "score": float}], "metadata": { ... } } — Redwood will validate the keys and types before returning the response so downstream parsers see deterministic shapes.

2) Streaming + early-stop: streaming will push partial tokens as they’re generated. For your reranking use-case we typically stream the final JSON object with a single flush at the end; if you want progressive UI updates we can stream incremental score summaries.

3) SDK changes: integration pattern options
- Minimal: Call Redwood generate() with streaming=true and a function schema. Client-side change = replace existing HTTP call with SDK call (1–2 dev days).
- Moderate: Add local prefix/KV caching and batch aggregator (3–5 dev days). We can provide a sample wrapper lib for your stack.

4) Benchmarks: please include payload size distribution and peak qps in the sample. If you can provide expected peak concurrent requests that will help us size Dedicated vs Hosted.

I’ve attached acme-mapping.csv as a starting point for field mappings. I’ll bring a short code snippet to the deep-dive showing the function-calling payload and a streaming example.

—Vivek
